resources.string: Scale a Yagi to another frequency or change element diameters.
What do you want to change?
Move to another frequency and scale diameters
Move to another frequency with specified diameters
Straight round elements from a model
Example of scaling mounted dimensions from 145 to 146 MHz. The driven element uses its assembled overall length. An NEC check requires a separate feed model.
Optional. Measure the driven element end to end, including the gap. With a gap, the driven element retains its proportional dimensions during a diameter correction.
Proportional scaling is available. Diameter correction and NEC checks require dimensions from a model.
Check the dimensions and their combination against the model limits.
This saved calculation cannot be reopened in this version. Its recorded dimensions remain in the project.

The diameter correction estimates the dimensions of straight round elements without boom correction. For a large diameter change, a long Yagi or frequencies above 144 MHz, verify by modelling and measurement.
This scaling assumes the mounting geometry changes in the same proportion.
λ is the wavelength at the target frequency. In combined mode L₁ and d₁ describe the proportionally scaled geometry, d₂ is the specified diameter and L₂ is the corrected length.

Frequency scaling is described by Hartmut Klüver (DG7YBN). Diameter correction is based on the formula by Günter Hoch (DL6WU) and Ian White (G3SEK), with the correction credited to Robin (G1YFG) by DG7YBN.
DG7YBN permits private construction and personal downloads. The original author specifies written consent for republishing complete designs and other protected materials listed in the terms.

Lengths, positions, diameters and the feed gap scale by the ratio of the original frequency to the target frequency.
At the original frequency, changing tubing diameter adjusts element lengths. Mounting distances stay the same.
The app first scales the geometry proportionally, then adjusts lengths for the specified diameters. To keep the existing tubing, enter its diameter.
Enter frequencies and dimensions or load the example.
Enter the full lengths of the reflector and driven element, and the distance between them. The new dimensions will appear below automatically.
Preliminary result. Check the attenuation at the new frequency.
λ₀ is the wavelength in free space. λ in cable is the shorter wavelength in the cable at the same frequency.
Matched line. The highlighted part of the scale shows the fraction of input power reaching the output.
At the load, |Γ| is the reflected-to-incident voltage amplitude ratio. Reflected power fraction is |Γ|².
Enter a default diameter or specify diameters in the element geometry. Individual values take priority.
Schematic illustration of a Yagi antenna before and after scaling.
